description:
FILED s451 (Fable, agent-Z review probes).  PRE-EXISTING on pre-round-10 main (probed at 4b7540b AND on the Z tree, identical): the %ENV/%INC MARKER does not survive the LIST-FLATTEN and REFERENT paths, so copying the environment wholesale is broken in three spellings while the keyed paths (exists/keys/each/delete/element read+write -- #701 s451z) are right:

    my %d = %ENV;             perl: full copy (78 keys)   PCL: ne (p-hash-= from the marker symbol copies nothing)
    my $r = \%ENV; my %v = %$r;   perl: full copy         PCL: DIES "Not a HASH reference" (%p-not-a-ref -- p-backslash of the marker makes a box p-cast-% rejects)
    my %h = %{"main::ENV"};   perl: full copy             PCL: 1 bogus pair (the marker itself flattened)

ONE mechanism: the consumers that expand a hash into PAIRS (p-hash-= source arm / the flattener) and p-backslash referent identity do not have the marker arm the keyed primitives have.  #701 added %p-hash-marker-p (rule 11) -- these are the remaining sites that should ask it and expand via the same env-walking arm keys/each already use.  The \%ENV referent also needs identity: perl says \%ENV == \%ENV and $$r{k} writes the real environment.

BAR: the three spellings + %INC twins vs perl; \%ENV element write-through; a die-arm audit that the #701 rule-12 die still fires only on the impossible state; io/+op/ single-file checks (env-reading suite files).  cl/-only expected.

DONE s452aa (Opus agent AA, round 11).

FIX = ONE new helper + one arm per consumer, all keyed on the existing
%p-hash-marker-p (#701's predicate, rule 11):

  %p-marker-pairs (marker) -> #(box(k) box(v) ...), walking the marker through
  p-keys + p-gethash, i.e. the SAME env/INC walk keys/each already use.

PAIR-EXPANDING consumers that now ask it:
  %p-flatten-list        (my %d = %ENV; my @a = (â¦, %ENV, â¦))
  p-flatten-args         (foo(%ENV) -> 2xN arguments)
  p-array-fill's add-items + %p-array-fill-item   (my @a = %ENV)
  p-array-init           ([%ENV], @{[%ENV]})
  p-hash-deref-=         (%$envref = (â¦) was a SILENT NO-OP; it now routes to
                          p-hash-fill, whose two PLACE arms already know how to
                          replace the process environment / the %INC table)
NOTE p-array-fill has its OWN walker on purpose (it preserves holes and stores
into PLACE), so the arm is spelled in both walkers, beside the sibling
hash-table-p arms -- not a drifted copy.
EVERY marker arm sits AFTER the aggregate fast paths: two EQ tests on the scalar
fallthrough, nothing on the hot path.

REFERENT half (the \%ENV spellings):
  p-backslash            wraps a marker exactly as it wraps a hash table, so the
                         referent IS the marker symbol -- EQ across calls, hence
                         \%ENV == \%ENV and a stable address, like a table's
  p-cast-% / p-ensure-hashref   pass the marker through, so %$r and $$r{k} reach
                         p-gethash's own %ENV arms (write-through works)
  p-ref / %p-ref-string / stringify-value   answer HASH / HASH(0xâ¦)
  %scalar-holds-ref-p    a scalar holding \%ENV is a REF, not a SCALAR
  %p-wrong-referent-p    a marker counts as a HASH referent, so @$envref dies
                         "Not an ARRAY reference" like perl

MEASUREMENT: 30 probes vs perl 5.40.3, ALL identical.  Before: 15 of 17 in the
first set diverged (A count:1 / DIED / C count:1 / D 1 / E 1 / F missing / G
DIED / H missing / I SCALAR SCALAR SCALAR / J u u / K DIED / L missing / O u)
and 3 of 13 in the second ("$r" printed %ENV-MARKER%; %$r = (C=>3) was a no-op;
@{[%ENV]} was one element).  Shapes covered: my %d = %ENV; \%ENV == \%ENV;
$$r{k} read AND write-through (verified against the real environment with a
backtick child); %$r; %{"main::ENV"}; my @a = %ENV; foo(%ENV); the %INC twins of
all of those; ref(); "$r"; (%ENV, FOO=>1); exists/keys/values/delete through the
ref; %ENV = %ENV; a copy is a COPY (writing the copy does not touch the
environment); scalar(%ENV); @{[%ENV]}; a count in list context; and the negative
@$envref -> "Not an ARRAY reference".

RULE-12 AUDIT: %p-symref-hash's die (added by #701) is untouched and still fires
only on the impossible state -- a symbol bound to something that is neither a
hash table nor a known marker.  The new %p-sysopen-direction die is #730's, not
this one's.

BAR LEGS: cold gate green; named sweep files chdir.t/each.t/local.t/magic.t
EXACTLY their pass-baseline rows (25/0, 51/0, 303/13, 152/37); twelve named
companion files incl. op/magic.t, op/leaky-magic.t, op/gmagic.t, uni/stash.t ALL
SAME as their snapshot rows.  cl/-only, so corpus-diff cannot see it and did not
need to.
